claim: Mars looks red because iron in its rocks, soil and dust has oxidized (rusted), and wind-lifted dust makes the whole planet look red from afar.

beats.caption: Brown, gold and tan
beats.vo: Look closer and Mars isn't one color. NASA says the surface is brown, gold, and tan, not bright red.

beats.caption: Iron + oxygen = rust
beats.vo: The red comes from iron. Iron minerals in Mars's rocks, soil, and dust have oxidized, which means they've rusted, just like an old nail.

beats.caption: Rusty dust paints the planet
beats.vo: Winds kick that rusty dust into the air, and from far away it makes the whole planet look red. So is Mars really the Red Planet, or the rusty one?

sources.text: NASA Science, Mars Facts: Mars looks reddish due to oxidization (rusting) of iron in its rocks, regolith and dust; the surface shows brown, gold and tan; dust lifted into the atmosphere makes the planet appear mostly red from a distance. https://science.nasa.gov/mars/facts/
